I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize cycle, because that is the most familiar and steady way for me to use my 19.1 mu in Quzhou County. I have 15 years of farming experience, I have well irrigation, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I will choose a plan that is reliable and not too labor-heavy. I will put 15.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 4.1 mu for cotton. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stability. For wheat and maize, I will use medium fertilizer rates and make sure irrigation is done at the key stages, because with irrigation I do not want to risk yield loss from dry weather. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area because it needs more pest control and more management, but I will still plant it because it spreads my risk and gives me another source of income. I will mostly use rotary tillage, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat to save time and labor.
